claim: About 15.4% of serious independent app developers generate at least $1,000 of current gross monthly revenue across their owned portfolio.
calculation_or_trace: Monte Carlo: selected subscription ever-hit rate x persistence x transfer factor, then portfolio aggregation.
caveat: 8.36%-25.02% plausible interval; not a census.

claim: About 10.2% of serious independent apps generate at least $1,000 of current gross monthly revenue.
caveat: 5.26%-17.44% plausible interval.

claim: Across all listed apps, roughly 1.0% clear $1,000 in a current month.
calculation_or_trace: Mixture of inactive, active-light, monetized-light, serious, and mature app states.
caveat: 0.31%-2.74%; denominator composition is uncertain.

claim: Sustaining $1,000 for three consecutive months is less common than touching it once.
calculation_or_trace: Current-month draws multiplied by persistence factors.
caveat: Three-month persistence is assumed, not directly observed store-wide.

claim: RevenueCat reports that 17.3% of newly launched apps in its selected cohort hit $1,000 monthly revenue within two years.
caveat: It is ever-hit, subscription-only, RevenueCat-integrated, active, and minimum-threshold selected.

claim: Only 4.6% of that RevenueCat launch cohort hit $10,000 monthly revenue within two years.
caveat: Not a store-wide prevalence estimate.

claim: The RevenueCat year-one monthly-revenue median is about $72, versus $2,574 at the 90th percentile.
caveat: Selected subscription apps; median versus right tail.

claim: Adapty reports the top 10% of observed subscription apps capture 94.5% of subscription revenue.
caveat: Vendor cohort and marketing framing; denominator/exclusions matter.

claim: Adapty’s concentration statistic implies the average top-decile app produces about 155 times the revenue of the average bottom-90% app.
caveat: Ratio of group averages, not median app performance.

claim: More than 90% of Play-distributing developers generated no revenue through Google Play Billing in CMA evidence.
caveat: Does not mean no ad, external-payment, physical-goods, or cross-platform revenue.

claim: Apple listed 2,172,472 apps in 2025, but 1,365,649 appeared in top-10 results for at least 1,000 searches during the year.
caveat: Search visibility is an activity proxy, not monetization.

claim: On Google Play, 83% of listed apps had fewer than three ratings as of July 14, 2026.
caveat: Ratings are a noisy activity proxy and AppBrain is not Google.

claim: The denominator changes the answer by more than an order of magnitude.
value: App: 0.98% all listed vs. 10.23% serious; developer: 1.55% vs. 15.41%
caveat: The contrast is modeled; direction is robust, exact magnitude is not.

claim: $9.99/month requires about 101 active subscribers for $1,000 gross, 118 for $1,000 proceeds at a 15% fee, and 140 for $1,000 owner profit under a lean cost model.
caveat: Ignores tax/refunds; profit model assumes $150 fixed and $0.25/subscriber variable cost.

claim: At RevenueCat’s overall D60 RPI of $0.34, a launch cohort needs about 2,941 installs to accumulate $1,000 by day 60.
caveat: Cumulative cohort revenue, not monthly recurring revenue.

claim: A base advertising app needs about 9,259 MAU for $1,000 monthly ad revenue.
calculation_or_trace: 1000/(12 sessions x 2 ads x 90% fill x $5 eCPM / 1000).
caveat: All ad inputs are scenarios; actual eCPMs and engagement vary widely.

claim: iOS monetizes subscription installs earlier than Google Play in the RevenueCat cohort.
value: $0.42 vs. $0.16 D60 RPI; 2.6% vs. 0.9% D35 conversion
caveat: Long-run payer LTV narrows to $23.38 vs. $21.62.

claim: Public case studies cannot estimate prevalence because they are selected on disclosure, verification, or saleability.
caveat: Cases are retained for mechanisms and unit economics only.

claim: A 16-product disclosed portfolio generated $855 in the latest 30 days and $555 aggregate MRR, with multiple apps at zero.
caveat: Not representative; some products may not be mobile apps.

claim: GurjarApp reported 212k users but no current revenue and $100-$150 monthly costs.
calculation_or_trace: Verified revenue listing plus founder statement.
caveat: User count and cost are founder-supplied; revenue account is linked.
